description: Move every workspace package from effect@3.21.2 to effect@4.0.0 with no Effect 3 form, shim, or still-compiling old idiom left (US-662..US-670). Each story is one complete PR against main that passes the full gate: one switch PR led by characterization tests, one Effect 4 idiom pass per area (with Effect's HttpClient and an MCP server on effect/ai), then one definition of a valid Landofile across Lando, editors, and Standard Schema tools, command tracing with opt-in OTLP export and embedding hooks, and measured decoder compilation. spec-effect-v4.md is normative.

userStories.title: Run Lando on Effect 4.0.0
userStories.description: As a user, Lando runs on Effect 4 with the same behavior and at least the same speed, and nothing in the repo still uses an Effect 3 API.
acceptanceCriteria: On the base commit, record the spec §12 baseline in `progress.txt`. Then commit characterization tests for every applicable spec §8 row, passing on Effect 3, in the owning packages' test trees: build counts for each stateful layer; resource lifetime in `bootstrap-lifecycle.ts`; text and JSON failure output from both shells for a tagged failure, a defect, an interrupt, and combined failures; shell exit codes; `runProbe` attempts and virtual time under `TestClock`; telemetry drain, MCP queue shutdown, log-follow and renderer stream completion; JSON log keys; process exit with a hanging telemetry sink; equality-sensitive collection results, or a recorded zero.

Root `package.json` uses the object `workspaces` form with `catalog.effect` set to exactly `4.0.0`. Every workspace that imports `effect` declares `"effect": "catalog:"`, and the TypeScript devDependency is `^5.9.0`. A test under `core/test/build/` fails on any other `effect` specifier or any `@effect/*` dependency.

Every spec §4.1 to §4.5 and §7 row is applied across all packages, tests, scripts, generator templates (with regenerated outputs), docs code samples, and agent instructions. This includes: the eight `FiberRef`s (seven files; `volume-coordination.ts` holds two) become `Context.Reference`s, with tests for lock and volume re-entrancy, the event depth guard, redaction tokens in child fibers, provider selection under concurrency, nested invocation ids, and cwd ownership; the CLI and library shells use `runPromiseExit` and render the `Cause`; the schema AST walkers and JSON Schema pipeline (`sdk/src/schema/json-schema*.ts`, `landofile-authoring*.ts`, `deprecation.ts`, `plugins/lando3/src/model.ts`, `engine/src/lifecycle/subscriber-index.ts`) work on Effect 4 `SchemaAST`; decode failures format through `SchemaIssue` with the current `"<path>: <message>"` template; authored-input schemas use `optionalKey`; the scaffolded plugin source compiles and its tests pass.

Characterization tests pass, or each intended difference is recorded with its reason. Tests that asserted Effect 3 stock issue wording move to Effect 4 wording and are listed. Custom messages are unchanged.

Artifacts stay draft-07 through `JsonSchema.toDocumentDraft07`. The `scripts/schema-compatibility/` classifier compares meaning and normalizes generator representation (definitions location, `$ref` naming, generated check descriptions, key order), with fixture tests. `check:schema-compatibility` against the base reports no unexplained semantic change. A test fails when any authored-input artifact property accepts `null`.
`sdk/test/fixtures/sdk-mvp-surface.json` is regenerated. `sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md` records the Effect 4 contract move. The spec §11 amendments for US-662 are applied.

`bun run gate:pr` and the full `bun run test` pass. Nightly-tier suites pass when run by path. Live provider suites pass when `LANDO_TEST_PODMAN_SOCKET` connects. `docs:check`, `docs:test`, `lint:guides`, `check:guide-coverage`, `check:public-transcripts`, and `GUIDE_DRIFT_BASE_REF=origin/main bun run check:guide-drift` pass. `bun run dev:guides <guide> --once` passes with a positive count for each guide in the US-662 Guide Coverage row. The compiled binary builds and passes the relocated-binary smoke.
`progress.txt` records the post-switch measurements next to the baseline. Any regression names its cause and owning story.
userStories.notes: Target main. Commit order is in spec §3. Forms that still compile on Effect 4 are left for the idiom passes, which rewrite each area once. Class: switch.

userStories.title: Write the SDK and primitive packages in Effect 4 idiom, with Effect's HttpClient
userStories.description: As a plugin author, the SDK contracts and primitive packages read like current Effect documentation, and HTTP calls go through Effect's standard `HttpClient` with Lando's network trust built in.
acceptanceCriteria: The idiom pass is complete for `sdk`, `state-store`, `redaction`, `http-client`, `managed-file`, `telemetry`, `landofile`, and `container-runtime`.

`@lando/http-client` provides Effect's `effect/http` `HttpClient`, built with `HttpClient.make` over the existing Bun fetch egress, with trust still resolved per request from `ConfigService`. The SDK's own `@lando/core/HttpClient` contract is removed. Every consumer migrates, including `engine/src/services/json-fetch.ts`, `Downloader` (which keeps its contract and checksum verification), healthcheck, scanner, and plugins. `LandoPluginContext` exposes the client.

The `network` boundary rule also flags `effect/http` `FetchHttpClient` imports outside `http-client/src/**`, with fixtures. Each request is a span with method and redacted URL attributes. A private-CA fixture server test passes.
Secret-carrying values from `@lando/sdk/secrets` and `@lando/redaction` implement `Redactable`. A test logs and inspects one through Effect and asserts the redacted form.
The CLI composition provides `References.TracerEnabled` as `false`, proven by a test that a span created during a command is not recorded.
`sdk/AGENTS.md` and `core/AGENTS.md` state the three service shapes, layer naming, and tracing policy as durable rules. The spec §11 amendments for US-663 are applied.
`@lando/sdk/test` contract kits accept the new layer names, and `core/test/contract/plugin-abstraction-coverage.test.ts` passes. `sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md` records renamed and removed exports.
Add `docs/guides/plugins/http-requests.mdx`. The standard `sdk` and `user` gates pass.
userStories.notes: Target main. Class: sdk plus user.

userStories.title: Write the engine in Effect 4 idiom
userStories.description: As an operator reading a trace, every planner phase, app operation, lifecycle step, and provider call appears as a named span, and the engine reads like current Effect documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: The idiom pass is complete for all of `engine/src` and `engine/test`, including the `@lando/engine/testing/*` doubles.
`scripts/build-bootstrap-layers.ts` and `scripts/bootstrap-layer-renderers.ts` emit namespace-imported `layer` names, and the generated layers are regenerated.

The hand-rolled ordering and cycle detection move to `Graph`: build-step batching and its `Cycle` result in `engine/src/services/build-app-plan.ts` (consumed by `build-app-graph.ts`), service `dependsOn` cycles in `engine/src/services/dependency-validation.ts`, and feature activation cycles (`detectCycle`) in `engine/src/services/app-feature.ts`. Error tags and messages, including the reported cycle path and edges, are unchanged.

Planner phases are spans named `AppPlanner.<phase>`. Operations (`start`, `stop`, `rebuild`, `destroy`, and the rest) are spans with provider calls nested under them. A test runs one operation against the test provider with an in-memory `Tracer` and asserts the span tree shape.
A focused test drives a time-dependent engine path with `TestClock`.
Standard `main` gates pass.

userStories.title: Serve MCP through Effect's MCP server
userStories.description: As an agent, `lando mcp` speaks MCP 2025-06-18 with structured results, asks the person in my client before risky calls, and serves Lando state and schemas as resources, with the same safety limits as before.
acceptanceCriteria: `lando mcp` uses `McpServer.layerStdio` with protocols 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, and 2024-11-05. `@lando/renderer` implements Effect's `Stdio` contract over Bun stdin and stdout, so it stays the only terminal writer. The current inbound frame limit and its failure behavior are kept, proven by the existing oversize test.

Tools are registered from the existing catalog projection with `addTool`, after the allowlist is applied. Input schemas come from the catalog. `outputSchema` comes from the command result JSON Schemas. Results carry `structuredContent` with the redacted, bounded `CommandResultEnvelope`, plus a text fallback.

Confirmation through elicitation: When the client advertises elicitation and a call lacks `yes: true`, `requireConfirmation` asks through `McpServer.elicit` with a `{ confirm: boolean }` schema and a message naming the app and the consequence. Accept proceeds. Decline, cancel, or no answer within 120 seconds fails with `CommandConfirmationError` reason `declined`. Clients without elicitation keep the current `non-interactive` failure, and `yes: true` behaves as today. Elicitation never lifts a deny, and `app:destroy` stays forbidden by default.

Resources: `lando://app/config`, `lando://app/info`, `lando://apps`, `lando://doctor`, and the template `lando://schemas/{name}` with name completion from the public registry. Payloads reuse the existing result schemas and are redacted and bounded. App-scoped resources resolve through `resolveApp`/`AppSelector` and fail with the existing tagged errors.

Existing behavior keeps its tests green: the concurrency limit of 4, cancellation through `notifications/cancelled`, progress notifications, `pre-mcp-call` and `post-mcp-call` events, redaction, and bounds. New tests cover elicitation (accept, decline, timeout, no capability) and resources (listing, reading, completion, and redaction of a planted secret).
The hand-written JSON-RPC transport, reader, writer, and framing in `mcp/src` are deleted. The rest of the `mcp` package passes the idiom pass.
Update `docs/guides/agent-native/mcp.mdx`. The spec §11 amendments for US-665 are applied.
Standard `main` gates pass, plus guide gates.
userStories.notes: Target main. `effect/ai` is unstable; the exact catalog pin covers it. Class: user.

userStories.title: Write the renderer, data mover, and core in Effect 4 idiom
userStories.description: As an operator, every command runs under one named span with its lifecycle stages as children, and core composition reads like current Effect documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: The idiom pass is complete for `renderer`, `data-mover`, and `core`, including `core/src/cli/**`, `core/src/runtime/**`, the library API, `core/src/testing/**`, and their tests.

Each dispatched command runs under one root span named `lando <command-id>`, with init, run, and render stages as children. Attributes carry the command id and invocation id only. Renderer per-frame paths use `Effect.fnUntraced`.
Public `@lando/core/testing` renames are recorded in `sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md`.
Standard `main` gates pass.

userStories.title: Write bundled plugins and the plugin scaffold in Effect 4 idiom, and keep old forms out
userStories.description: As a plugin author, `lando plugin:new` and every bundled plugin show current Effect idiom. As a maintainer, old forms cannot creep back.
acceptanceCriteria: The idiom pass is complete for every bundled plugin under `plugins/*`.

`engine/src/operations/plugin-scaffold.ts` emits the spec §5 shapes and `Effect.fn`. A test scaffolds a plugin, then builds and tests it. `docs/guides/plugins/authoring-new-plugin.mdx` matches the scaffold, and its scenario passes with a positive count.

A new `effect-idioms` boundary rule scans the shared shipped-runtime tier and bans: `Data.TaggedError` and `Data.Error`; `Date.now()` and `new Date(` in modules that import `effect`; named functions or methods whose body only returns `Effect.gen(...)`; local definitions named `isRecord`, `isPlainObject`, or `isObject`; exports named `*Live`; imports from `@effect/*`. It has fixtures and tests, a seam-impossibility justification in `scripts/boundary/registry.ts`, and a `scripts/boundary/README.md` row. It passes on the whole repo.
The spec §11 amendment for US-667 is applied.
Standard `main` gates pass, plus guide gates.

userStories.title: Give Lando, editors, and other tools one definition of a valid Landofile
userStories.description: As a Landofile author, agent, or tool builder, one run reports every problem with its path and a fix hint. My editor flags the same problems as I type, and any Standard Schema consumer flags them too.
acceptanceCriteria: Diagnostics: Authored-file decoders run with `errors: "all"`, so one Landofile with three independent problems reports all three. `LandofileValidationError.issues`, and the matching recipe-manifest and include errors, become arrays of `{ path: Array<string | number>, message: string, suggestion?: string }`. `ConfigLintViolation` uses the same path form. Unknown keys get a `suggestion` naming the closest allowed key within edit distance 2, for example `imgae` suggests `image`. The text renderer prints one line per issue as `services.web.port: <message>`. The `--format=json` envelope and MCP results carry the structured `issues`.

Editor validation: Public artifacts under `dist/schemas/**` become draft 2020-12 documents. Editor artifacts `landofile.schema.json` and `global-config.schema.json` are emitted in draft-07 through `JsonSchema.toDocumentDraft07`, with `onExcessProperty: "error"` and `generateDescriptions: true`. One exported constant in `@lando/sdk/schema` holds the editor schema URL. The docs build publishes the artifact at that path, and a test asserts they agree. New Landofiles written by `lando init` and `lando app:config:translate` start with a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=<url>` line. Existing files are never rewritten for it.

Standard Schema: a tree-shakeable `@lando/sdk/schema/standard` subpath exports Standard Schema V1 plus Standard JSON Schema V1 views of the Landofile input, global config, plugin manifest, and recipe manifest schemas.

One parity test holds all three surfaces to Lando's decoder. The fixtures are every valid Landofile fixture under `docs/guides/**/fixtures` and `recipes/**`, plus a curated invalid set covering unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-range ports, and `null` for an optional key. The published documents, loaded with `SchemaRepresentation.fromJsonSchemaDocument`, and the Standard Schema views must agree with the decoder on accept or reject, at a positive count. Standard Schema issues match Lando's `issues` paths and messages. Checks JSON Schema cannot express are listed with a reason.
Update the SDK error schemas, `sdk/API_COMPATIBILITY.md`, snapshots, and compatibility exceptions. The spec §11 amendments for US-668 are applied.

Guides: Update `docs/guides/landofile/config-lint.mdx`, `docs/guides/scripting-with-json.mdx`, and `docs/guides/schemas/json-schema-artifacts.mdx`. Add `docs/guides/landofile/editor-validation.mdx` and `docs/guides/schemas/standard-schema.mdx`. Scenarios assert `issues[0].path` and its suggestion, the modeline in an `init` result, and a `~standard.validate` call from a Bun script.
Standard `sdk` and `user` gates pass.
userStories.notes: Target main. Class: sdk plus user.

userStories.title: Show where a command spends its time, locally or in your own tracing stack
userStories.description: As a user or agent chasing a slow command, `--trace` shows a timing tree. As a team with an observability stack, I can send traces to my collector. As an embedding host, Lando's spans, logs, and defects flow into my tooling. Lando never sends traces anywhere I did not configure.
acceptanceCriteria: `--trace`: A global `--trace` flag (and `LANDO_TRACE=1` through the env helper) enables the tracer on dispatcher-routed commands. The level-`none` fast path is untouched. A Lando `Tracer` keeps finished spans in a bounded buffer of 10,000 spans and counts the overflow. The text renderer prints a timing tree after the result, collapsing spans under 1% of total. `--format=json` adds a `trace` field typed by a new public `CommandTrace` schema with name, parent, start offset, duration, status, and attributes. The schema is registered in `JSON_SCHEMA_REGISTRY` with a contract fixture.

OTLP export: Global config gains `tracing.otlp.endpoint` and `tracing.otlp.headers`, with header values treated as secrets in config views. When unset, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` are read through the env helper. When configured, commands export spans with `OtlpTracer` and `OtlpSerialization.layerJson` over Lando's `HttpClient`, with resource attributes `service.name=lando`, `service.version`, OS, and architecture. Export is fire-and-forget. A failure never changes the exit status. The flush runs after the completion line and is bounded to 1 second. Nothing is exported when neither setting is present.

Embedding hosts: `openLandoRuntime` and `makeLandoRuntime` never override a host-provided `Tracer`, `References.CurrentLoggers`, `References.MinimumLogLevel`, or `ErrorReporter`. Spans from `runtime.run` and app handles parent to the host's current span. Operation boundaries use `Effect.withErrorReporting`, so defects (not tagged failures) reach the host reporter. The CLI shell installs a reporter that feeds the existing bug-report rendering, so both shells share one path.
Span attributes pass through `RedactionService` before retention or export.

Tests cover: a secret planted in env and flags reaching neither text, JSON, nor the exporter; a local `Bun.serve` OTLP receiver getting the spans; an unreachable endpoint leaving exit status and completion timing unchanged; an in-memory host tracer, logger, and reporter.
Without tracing, `bench:tooling-hot-path` stays within spec §12. With `--trace`, overhead is recorded.
Update the config schema, snapshots, and SDK compatibility. The spec §11 amendments for US-669 are applied.

Add `docs/guides/cli/trace-a-command.mdx`, `docs/guides/cli/export-traces.mdx`, and `docs/guides/library/embedding-observability.mdx`, linked from `verbosity-and-debug.mdx` and `embedding-runtime.mdx`. Scenarios assert `trace.spans` in JSON output and a host span parenting a Lando span.
Standard `main` gates pass, plus guide gates.

userStories.title: Compile hot-path schema decoders when it measurably helps
userStories.description: As a user, tooling commands that decode cached plans and Landofiles get faster when ahead-of-time compiled decoders measurably help, and nothing changes when they do not.
acceptanceCriteria: Measure decode time of the app-plan cache, the command cache, and Landofile decode on the tooling hot path, first with the interpreter and then with `SchemaAOTCompiler` output. Record both in `progress.txt`.

Adopt AOT output only if `bench:tooling-hot-path` p95 improves by at least 5 ms or 10%. The compiled decoders become a `derived` codegen catalog entry, never committed. A test proves compiled and interpreted decoders agree on the US-668 valid and invalid fixture sets. The compiled binary still builds.
If the bar is not met, ship no code change. Record the numbers and the decision.
Standard `main` gates pass.
